experienceSection.title: Experience

roles.summary: Built retrieval, transactional, and data systems for Tmall Campus, a digital-services ecosystem serving 800+ universities and nearly 20 million students.

caseStudy.label: Context
caseStudy.text: Worked across campus knowledge search, shopping discovery, user-profile data, and venue-booking workflows where model quality and service reliability had to be evaluated separately.

caseStudy.label: System
caseStudy.text: Combined sparse and dense retrieval, offline evaluation, batch profile processing, PostgreSQL transactions, and observable event delivery rather than treating the work as a single model endpoint.

caseStudy.label: Validation
caseStudy.text: Used labeled retrieval sets, a 1,000-request ranking evaluation, concurrency tests, backend and browser tests, and regression cases to verify behavior before production selection.

highlights: Built a Python retrieval service and benchmark covering 778 entries and 6,562 queries. Comparing BM25, BGE, and reciprocal-rank fusion led to BGE selection at 76.40% Top-1 and 91.34% Top-3 accuracy.
Combined ItemCF, field-aware BM25, dense embeddings, and weighted reciprocal-rank fusion, improving ranking-stage Recall@10 from 70% to 85% in a 1,000-request offline evaluation.
Transformed 100M raw interactions into 86.3M training records for 987,992 users, isolating offline computation from latency-sensitive online profile reads.

Implemented idempotent venue booking with PostgreSQL and SQLAlchemy transactions, a FIFO waitlist, transactional outbox, and leader leases. A 20-request concurrency test produced one successful admission, 19 conflict rejections, and zero overselling.

roles.summary: Investigating how software-engineering agents generate, retain, and abandon localization hypotheses across multi-step trajectories.

caseStudy.label: Question
caseStudy.text: A final pass or fail score does not explain whether an agent never formed the right hypothesis, selected the wrong action, or abandoned a correct direction later.

caseStudy.label: Method
caseStudy.text: Extract and track hypotheses from reasoning trajectories, then label generation, selection, and execution failures at the step level.

caseStudy.label: Evaluation
caseStudy.text: Compare four search policies across localization quality, patch correctness, hypothesis survival, and token and step cost on 50 verified instances.

highlights: Analyzing 50 SWE-bench Verified Mini instances with mini-swe-agent to classify generation, selection, and execution failures.
Building a trajectory-level hypothesis-tracking framework that records when plausible localization hypotheses emerge, survive, or disappear.
Separating search quality from final patch correctness so policy comparisons reveal how an agent reached its outcome, not only whether the patch passed.

roles.summary: Built a full-stack AI education platform that generates structured textbooks through a six-stage LLM workflow and lets users query and edit content with an agentic page assistant.

caseStudy.label: Context
caseStudy.text: Textbook generation is a long-running, multi-output workflow. Users need durable progress, visible intermediate results, and reliable in-page edits instead of waiting on one opaque request.

caseStudy.label: Architecture
caseStudy.text: A provider-agnostic six-stage workflow persists content state in PostgreSQL, runs work through Django, Celery, and Redis, and streams text and tool events into editable React blocks.

caseStudy.label: Reliability
caseStudy.text: Dependency-aware scheduling, retries, durable job state, failure recovery, focused tests, fault injection, and full-section context propagation address both backend and editing failures.

highlights: Built a six-stage workflow that turns a topic into textbook content, exercises, code, images, and video while supporting OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, and Grok through one interface.
Separated long-running generation from web requests with Celery and Redis, persisted execution state in PostgreSQL, and synchronized progress through Django Channels, Redis, and WebSockets.
Developed a 28-tool Page Assistant with native function calling and conversation memory, using a stable block contract so generated output remains directly editable in React.
Resolved long-form editing failures by removing a 1,000-character truncation and propagating full-section context through the editing path.

roles.summary: Building a local-first AI execution coach for adaptive task planning and recovery; selected for the Alibaba Tmall Campus One Person Company (OPC) student entrepreneurship program.

caseStudy.label: Product Problem
caseStudy.text: Plans break when priorities shift or attention drifts. The product must preserve completed work, identify what changed, and produce a useful next action instead of restarting the plan.

caseStudy.label: Execution Model
caseStudy.text: Multimodal inputs become a versioned task DAG with explicit dependencies, insertions, deferrals, validation, state reconciliation, deterministic fallback, and undo.

caseStudy.label: Privacy Boundary
caseStudy.text: A local-first architecture keeps raw activity data on device, applies pre-inference privacy filters, and routes only eligible work to local or cloud models.

highlights: Built a Gemma-powered multimodal pipeline that turns PDFs, screenshots, and notes into structured task DAGs for planning, progress tracking, and recovery.
Implemented dependency-aware replanning with task insertion, deferral, validation, state reconciliation, deterministic fallback, and undo so schedule changes do not erase completed work.
Shipped React, Node.js, Express, and SSE prototypes across web and macOS or Windows, with activity classification, model routing, provider failover, and real-time feedback.
Extended the product with the ADTI attention-personality test, 16 original character identities, and a desktop companion that visualizes progress and guides recovery.

roles.summary: Developed AI workflows, backend services, and evaluation capabilities for a policy-grounded expense-audit copilot.

caseStudy.label: Context
caseStudy.text: Expense review required evidence from receipts, reports, policies, and internal APIs. Recommendations needed to remain traceable to policy rather than rely on free-form model judgment.

caseStudy.label: System
caseStudy.text: A LangChain retrieval pipeline grounds decisions in company policy, while typed FastAPI and Pydantic services separate stateless audit logic from policy and receipt storage.

caseStudy.label: Evaluation
caseStudy.text: Structured outputs, function schemas, health checks, Dockerized services, and MLflow comparisons made reliability, retrieval quality, latency, and cost visible before release.

highlights: Built an expense-audit service that analyzes receipts and reports, validates transaction details, and generates policy-grounded approve, review, or reject recommendations, reducing median review time from 6.4 to 2.1 minutes per report.
Implemented policy retrieval with document chunking, OpenAI embeddings, vector search, and context-grounded generation to keep recommendations tied to company rules.

Used structured outputs and function calling to extract receipt fields, flag missing data, query internal expense APIs, and recognize duplicate queries. Average tool calls fell from 2.5 to 1.6 per audit and token cost fell by 36%.
Designed a modular FastAPI and Pydantic backend with typed validation, error handling, structured logging, health checks, Docker packaging, and MLflow evaluation pipelines.

entries.title: Cost-Aware Active Failure Diagnosis
entries.subtitle: Applied AI Systems Research · Summer 2026
metaLines: Research project under the guidance of Prof. Kalev Kask
entries.lead: A decision-support system for diagnosing software-service failures when the available evidence is incomplete, noisy, or misleading.
entries.body: Co-developed a leakage-controlled research pipeline spanning root-cause classification, retrieval-augmented diagnosis, and cost-aware diagnostic action selection. The study evaluates eight balanced root-cause categories across 32 independent scenarios and 384 deterministic incident variants, with six offline action-selection policies and four scenario-group cross-validation folds.
entries.result: A learned Selective RAG gate preserved the accuracy of Always-RAG on Qwen 9B (0.794 vs. 0.792) while reducing retrieval invocation from 100% to 34.4%, harmful switches from 14 to 6, and estimated sequential latency from 4.050s to 2.703s.
entries.technology: Python · RAG · Qwen · Ollama · TF-IDF · Logistic Regression · Pytest
